mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up numerical integration on GDC

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Numerical integration using a Graphic Display Calculator (GDC).
step_by_step: Enter the function $\sqrt{x} e^{x^2}$ into the numerical integration tool on the calculator.
Set the lower limit to $0$ and upper limit to $2$.
Read the output $\approx 20.7380$ and round to 3 significant figures.

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up numerical integration in radian mode

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Numerical integration of a non-elementary antiderivative using GDC.
step_by_step: Ensure the calculator angle mode is set to radians.
Obtain $3.76578\dots$ and round to 3 significant figures.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Evaluating trigonometric functions in degree mode rather than radian mode.

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up numerical integration in radian mode

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Numerical integration of radical and trigonometric expression using GDC.
step_by_step: Verify the calculator is in radian mode.
Read calculator output $2.16295\dots$ and round to 3 significant figures.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Degree mode instead of radian mode.
